scope: Compared full Japanese source and twelve translations, Windows command syntax, parameter case, executable scope/path, credential handling, unattended-access caveats, publication dates, and references.
findings: Removed duplicate future date; retained 2023-01-13 and set lastmod 2026-11-24.
Corrected password parameter from undocumented uppercase -P to documented lowercase -p; TeamViewer states command parameters are case-sensitive.
Clarified this example is for the full Windows version and that omitting -p prompts for a password unless Easy Access is available.
Added a warning that a password-bearing shortcut stores the password in readable form and added TeamViewer safer unattended-access guidance.
Updated the official command-line reference URL and localized the safety guidance across twelve translations.

post/TeamViewerで簡単リモート接続/index.en.md.summary: Compared the complete Japanese article and all twelve translations with current official TeamViewer command-line and security documentation. Corrected the case-sensitive password flag, limited the example to the full Windows version, explained optional password behavior, and warned against storing credentials in readable shortcuts.

meaning.note: Compared the connection workflow and explained the difference between an interactive password prompt and Easy Access for unattended access.

terminology.note: Verified Windows full version, partner ID, password flag -p (case-sensitive), Easy Access, allowlist, and multi-factor authentication terminology against TeamViewer documentation.

code.note: Replaced -P with the documented case-sensitive -p, retained the Windows executable path as a placeholder example, and checked all 13 localized command samples.

links.note: Replaced the old community article URL with TeamViewer’s current official command-line documentation and added official unattended-access and security references.

limitations: AI-assisted review; no human or native-speaker certification.
The executable path can vary by installation; the example is for the full Windows version.
The command supports password input, but a shortcut that contains a password exposes it in readable text; safer unattended-access configuration depends on account and device settings.
